Not a voucher. 5 Claude prompts for flights, bags and money abroad. Swipe ▸

slides.title: Cash, *not a voucher*
slides.prompt: My airline canceled or changed my flight. Here is their email, booking number blacked out. Tell me if this counts as a significant change under US DOT rules. Then write a short reply that turns down the new flight and the voucher and asks for a refund to my original payment.
slides.why: Canceled, or moved 3+ hours (6+ international), and you decline? You are owed your money back. Card refunds: 7 business days.

slides.title: Late bag, *fee back*
slides.prompt: My checked bag reached me [hours] hours after my [domestic or international] flight landed. Here is my bag fee receipt and the delay report. Write a short, polite request to the airline for my bag fee back that names the US DOT rule.
slides.why: US rule: your bag fee comes back if the bag is 12+ hours late on a domestic flight, 15 to 30 hours on international.

slides.title: Beat the *24 hour clock*
slides.prompt: Here is my flight confirmation. Tell me when I booked, whether that was at least 7 days before departure, and the exact time my free cancellation ends. Then list every other cancel deadline in my hotel and car bookings.
slides.why: Booked with the airline 7+ days out? It must let you cancel free within 24 hours or hold the fare. Travel sites may differ.

slides.title: Pay in *their money*
slides.prompt: I am going to [country]. Here are my card's terms. In 3 short lines: what should I tap when a card machine or ATM asks if I want to pay in US dollars or local currency, and what does my card charge on foreign purchases?
slides.why: Pick local currency. Paying in dollars lets the shop or ATM set the rate, often 3% or more worse.

slides.title: Check your *passport*
slides.prompt: I am a [nationality] citizen flying to [countries] from [date] to [date]. My passport expires on [date]. For each country, list what I must check: passport validity, visa or entry permit, blank pages. Link only official government sites and flag anything I should confirm.
slides.why: Many countries want your passport valid 6 months past your trip. US travelers: check each country page on travel.state.gov.

cta.gift: Your free refund guide: the flight refund rule and copy and paste refund requests.
cta.small: Free in your DMs. *US rules. Not legal advice.*

bg_facts: Canceled flight and you decline? You are owed a refund.
Bag fee back if the bag is 12+ hours late domestic.
Booked 7+ days out: cancel free within 24 hours or hold.
